chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: Buster Smith's reluctance to travel and his recent playing
summary: Smith won't fly and is superstitious; Durham describes seeing him at the Kansas City concert and a Decca record they made together.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, why was it then that -- you know, with this talent, why was it that he seemed as though he always wanted to stay at home?
Buster?
Yeah. I mean, he never --
Well, he don't like to travel.
Oh.
He won't fly at all.
Oh.
He ain't particular about busses and things, boats. He rides a bus or a train, but he wouldn't fly even to Kansas City. He's a superstitious type of fellow.
What?
Superstitious type of fellow, and he ain't got a hair on his head, not a grey hair in his head, right today.
He's your age, isn't he?
No. No, not that type of aging. He don't look old, because I came --
But, I mean, he's as old as you, isn't he?
Yeah, he's a little older than me, about 72. And I came in and I sat right beside him in -- right
down in a seat beside him, and I got up and said, when is Buster Smith coming in? Everybody started laughing, place was packed. Joe Thomas was there --
Oh, this is when you did this Kansas City --
He said, you ain't going to speak to your buddy? You just got up beside him. I didn't (inaudible), so we stayed together. But the guy is terrific.
He still plays?

Yeah, he plays a -- he doesn't -- I was thinking about bringing him here and letting him work out back. He plays bass, he played piano in a concert. Did one number for me, and after that, (inaudible) not playing no more. He say, go ahead, I will find any number for anybody. So he played for Bud and all the other thing. (Inaudible) he was at the piano and he just played anything.
Did you hear that record he made about five or six years ago?
Well, he made something with me, I know. Thing like Morton Swing and that stuff.
When did he make them? Oh, you mean, that was for Decca.
Yeah, yeah.
